note: Frozen read API. This static site renders this snapshot; run the Go backend for live data.

/api/v1/alpha?days=90.note: Upper bound is perfect hindsight minus the best single venue, i.e. the entire value of routing with a crystal ball. A realistic keeper captures a fraction of it.

/api/v1/carry.note: Real one-year return of a dollar deposited at each country's central bank rate, converted back to dollars at today's rate. Uses the actual currency path, not a forecast. A managed currency can post a low volatility and still step sharply; the drawdown column exists for that. Not an offer, not advice, and not a product: no cross-border deposit is available through Keelson.

strategies.label: Chase the headline rate
strategies.note: Every month, move to whichever country advertises the highest rate. The intuitive strategy, and the one the advert wants.

strategies.label: Chase the net return, monthly
strategies.note: Every month, move to whichever country actually paid the most in dollars the month before — after the currency moved.

strategies.label: Chase the net return, quarterly
strategies.note: The same rule, but only allowed to move once a quarter. Fewer moves, less whipsaw, and the number we would actually ship.

strategies.label: Rank once, then leave it alone
strategies.note: Mexico won the first quarter on net return (4.29%) and was then left alone for the rest of the year. Rank the countries on the first three months, put the money in the winner, and do not touch it again. No hindsight, no churn — the honest test of whether the ranking is useful.

strategies.label: Pick the winner in hindsight
strategies.note: Türkiye, held for the whole window. Impossible in advance; the number to beat.

strategies.label: Leave the dollars alone
strategies.note: The baseline: dollars earning the US rate. No currency risk, nothing to watch.

/api/v1/cherry.note: Net return is what a dollar actually earned: the local central bank rate, multiplied by the currency's actual move against the dollar, minus our fee, measured against US inflation. This is a measurement of public data, not a product: we cannot open a deposit in another country for you, and nothing here is an offer.

/api/v1/decisions.note: Every check we made, including the ones where we did nothing. A log that only shows the moves that worked is advertising, not a log.

/api/v1/meta.automation: policy-bounded: the vault enforces caps, cooldowns and a NAV check
/api/v1/meta.custody: non-custodial: the backend holds no key and signs nothing

chosen_by_measurement.cooldown_secs: average leadership between the two verified venues was ~6.7 days; a 7-day cooldown missed most switches
chosen_by_measurement.max_venue_share_of_cap: capped at 2% of a venue so our own exit does not become the risk
chosen_by_measurement.min_capacity_usd: venues under $100k cannot absorb our exit without moving the rate against us
chosen_by_measurement.min_improvement_bps: below 25 bps the switch costs more attention than it earns

/api/v1/policy.explain: These parameters are what a user signs once. The vault cannot exceed them, and the keeper cannot bypass them.

incidents.note: Aug 2026: a pool that acts as the safety cushion for every Blend pool was drained. Every cushion was hit at once and the chain's lending market lost about 60% of its size within a day. This is why we never put money in the cushions.

Feb 2026: the price feed this pool relies on was pushed around using a market with almost no depth. About $10.9M was lost. Not a bug in Blend's own code, but every pool built like this one leans on the same feed.
